newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WARNE STRIKES IN FIERCE BATTLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WARNE STRIKES IN FIERCE BATTLE.

text.p: Australian wrist spinner Shane Warne struck an important blow to remove experienced West Indies batsman Carl Hooper during an intense battle for domination in the second test on Sunday.
At lunch on the third day at the Sydney Cricket Ground, West Indies were 223 for four, 108 runs adrift of Australia's first innings 331 but with six wickets in hand.
West Indies added a meagre 67 runs during the morning session against an accurate and unyielding Australian bowling attack for the loss of Hooper.
The tourists, who lost the first test in Brisbane by 123 runs, reached 200 in the 86th over of the innings.
But despite their slow progress on Sunday, their batting showed the resolve needed to build a first innings lead against bowlers capable of applying relentless pressure.
Hooper began the day on 27 and faced 34 balls without adding to his overnight score before being trapped leg before wicket by Warne without playing a shot with the total on 166.
Shivnarine Chanderpaul was equally cautious in advancing his score from three to 41 not out during the morning session. Jimmy Adams was the other not out batsman on 25.
Fast bowler Glenn McGrath, who dismissed opener Robert Samuels for 35 and Brian Lara for two on Saturday, highlighted the early domination enjoyed by Australia.
In his opening spell of seven overs, McGrath did not conceded a single run off the bat, slowing the scoring rate to a crawl.
Warne was a little more expensive during an 11-over spell that cost 24 runs.
West Indies opener Sherwin Campbell provided the platform for the innings by hitting 77 on Saturday before being bowled by an inswinging yorker from all-rounder Greg Blewett.
